title: dhoby-ghaut: GPU rendering for the 3D and 2D views (sphere impostors for pebbles; GPU or accelerated CSG ray tracing)
abstract:
Part of #561. Maintainer, 2026-10-05: "why is the 2D and 3D rendering slow, are there not shaders available?" Measured: a full-resolution HTR-10 half-section ray trace takes 5-7 s (16-core machine, Xvfb). Cause: both views use outram-blender's CPU port of OpenMC's ray tracer / slice plotter; every pixel walks the CSG through nested lattices (core lattice -> pebble -> TRISO) with no BVH. outram-blender has no GPU rendering (its only wgpu code is a vertex-transform compute kernel) and no CSG tessellator, so there is nothing for a rasteriser to draw.

Proposed, in order:
1. **Pebble views (DEM pour, bed overview):** instanced sphere impostors in an egui wgpu paint callback (one quad per pebble, sphere shading + depth in the fragment shader). 27 000 pebbles at interactive rates. This draws DEM centres, not solver geometry, and must be labelled so.
2. **Solver-geometry views and the review gate** (must stay a trace of the assembled geometry, drawing HARD RULE): either a WGSL ray-marcher over the CSG primitives (quadrics, planes, rect/hex lattices, translations) with a CPU parity test against the OpenMC-parity plotter, or a BVH / lattice-aware acceleration of the CPU tracer. Pixel parity with the existing tracer is the acceptance gate.
